sort_pointer_flow: Each arm supplies the matching family comparator in rsi, stable-sort helper in r8 and insertion helper in r9. Dispatcher saves these in -0x38/-0x48/-0x30(rbp). Insertion branch invokes saved r9; stable branch invokes saved r8; comparator is forwarded through rcx. Comparator bodies use fixed-width comparisons without calls; sorting helpers retain indirect comparator calls.

V4.compaction: 0x1c0180/184 stores completed range at sorted rbx + rcx*8; 0x1c01cb/1cf stores final range.
V4.count_branch: 0x1c01d4 forms completed count+1 in rsi; 0x1c01d8 compares sorted count from rdx; 0x1c01db branches to 0x1c0273 returning sorted rbx when count is unchanged.
V4.fresh_result: 0x1c01e1 loads empty storage into rcx; edi=0/edx=0; 0x1c01ec calls capacity helper with resultCount in rsi.
V4.copy: 0x1c0210 loads 8-byte records from sorted rdi; 0x1c022e writes new rax buffer. Counter r12 starts -1; increment/compare at 0x1c0234/23a copies completedCount+1 records.
V4.ownership: At 0x1c026b new result rax transfers to rbx; 0x1c026e releases sorted rdi; 0x1c0273 returns result.

V6.compaction: 0x1c03ee..401 completed and 0x1c0462..475 final stores use sorted rbx with index*32.
V6.count_branch: 0x1c047a forms completed count+1 in r14; 0x1c047e compares sorted count; 0x1c0481 branches to 0x1c0554 returning sorted rbx when count is unchanged.
V6.fresh_result: 0x1c0487 loads empty storage into rcx; edi=0/edx=0; r14 passes as rsi to capacity helper at 0x1c0498.
V6.copy: 0x1c04c0..4cf loads four 8-byte words; 0x1c04ee..4fd writes new result. Offset advances32 and resultCount r14 decrements until zero at 0x1c0502..509.
V6.ownership: 0x1c0549 saves sorted rbx in rdi; 0x1c054c assigns new result rax to rbx; 0x1c054f releases sorted; 0x1c0554 returns new result.

baseline_contrast: Both baseline families load sorted count into rsi before their first separate-result capacity helper (V4 0x1c01b6 -> call0x1c01cb; V6 0x1c037e -> call0x1c0397).
allocation_helper_observations: The reduced-result call passes empty storage, resultCount and growForAppend=false. The helper selects max(requestedCount, sourceCount=0), allocates 8*count+32 bytes for V4 or 32*count+32 for V6, then derives capacity using malloc_usable_size. Copy/move branches and source release remain in the helper; coalescers retain conditional copy-on-write and append-capacity fallback branches.
limitations: These findings cover the captured ordinary concrete Array CLI paths, not every generic caller.
Calls to release end this coalescer ownership; this does not prove immediate physical memory reclamation.
Requested allocation bytes and capacity rounding do not establish total live allocation count, RSS, steady-state memory, or throughput.
Input storage, sort scratch and allocator behavior remain separate.
Observed three candidate/one baseline uniqueness sites describe these exact frozen function bodies only.
